newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - United says Blenheim to enhance earnings.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - United says Blenheim to enhance earnings.

text.p: United News & Media Plc said on Tuesday that it expects the acquisition of British exhibitions organiser Blenheim Group Plc to be earnings enhancing in the first full year.

United made an agreed offer for Blenheim of 5.00 stg a share, valuing the company at 592.5 million stg. "The acquisition will be earnings enhancing in the first full year, but the real attraction is the long term growth we can get out by combining these businesses into one group," Clive Hollick, chief executive of United, said in a telephone interview.
Market talk that United was close to securing a deal with Blenheim had gathered pace in recent days and the announcement ends months of speculation over who would actually buy Blenheim.

United and Anglo-Dutch group Reed Elsevier had long been seen as rival suitors. But Dutch publisher VNU forced the issue with a market raid last week, paying five pounds a share for 15 percent of Blenheim. United said it has already secured acceptances for 51 percent of the exhibitions group.
VNU responded to United's purchase by saying that it would not make a counter bid for Blenheim.

"This is the first major move that we have made since the (MAI) merger. We stated very clearly that we wanted to build up our core businesses to positions of market leadership and this makes us the world's largest exhibition group," said Hollick. United, which also publishes British national newspapers The Daily Express and the Daily Star, said the combination of Miller Freeman with Blenheim produced pro forma turnover of 545.5 million stg and operating profit of 88.0 million. Miller Freeman is the business magazines and exhibitions arm of United News. It operates in the U.S., Europe and Asia.

Blenheim chairman, Neville Buch, said, "I wish Clive Hollick every success, Blenheim is an excellent company with first class people. The price fully reflects its value and the work we have all put into creating it."

Analysts had long viewed Blenheim as an ideal fit for United News given Blenheim's strength in Europe and France in particular, while the American market is regarded as the main strength of Miller Freeman.

"It (Blenheim) has an extremely attractive portfolio of trade shows which provide us with a very good fit in terms of the area of the markets they cover," Hollick told Reuters. Hollick said that United was only really prepared to make a move on Blenheim after the announcment of its half year results on October 2.
Blenheim made pre-tax profit of 30.7 million stg in the six months to June 30, 1996, on turnover of 102.8 million.
United News shares were up 17p at 670-1/2 by 0828 GMT, while Blenheim shares rose 24p to 497-1/2.
